business_scope.primary_industry_name: Digital Magazine Publishing and Sponsored Media Placements

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified system based on Swiss Civil Code of 1907 and Swiss Code of Obligations of 1911; cantonal procedural and notarial law variations)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: [FTA] EFTA Convention (1960, amended 2021; Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein)
[FTA] EU-Switzerland Bilateral Agreements I and II (1999-2004; market access for services incl. digital media)
[DTAA] Switzerland-United States Tax Convention (1996, amended by 2009 Protocol; FATCA exchange)
[FTA] Switzerland-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (in force 1 July 2019; covers e-commerce and digital services)
[BIT] Swiss-Chinese Bilateral Investment Treaty (2009, superseding 1986 BIT)
[FTA] WTO GATS commitments (WTO member since 1995; digital publishing and advertising services)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220) Art. 626i-626j, Art. 927a and Art. 932j as amended by the Federal Act on the Implementation of FATF Recommendations (in force 1 November 2023; UBO declarations to the Swiss Federal Central Tax Office with transitional filing deadline 31 December 2024); Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing of 10 October 1997 (AMLA/GwG, SR 955.0) Art. 2a, Art. 3-4, Art. 9; FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance of 25 November 2015 (AMLO-FINMA, SR 955.033.0); FINMA Circular 2023/01 'Financial Crime'; Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0) Art. 305bis-305ter; Federal Act on the Implementation of International Sanctions of 22 March 2002 (Embargo Act, SR 946.231).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Statuten) executed as deed of formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the canton of the registered office (public law notariat)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Mandatory notarial certification; if a foreign execution element exists, Hague Apostille by competent foreign authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity document of each shareholder, director and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil or passport authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent foreign authority; consular legalization if the country of origin is not an Apostille Convention member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or excerpt of foreign commercial register (required for any corporate shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction (e.g., Companies House, Delaware Division of Corporations)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus certified German, French, Italian or English translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration form (declaration of the beneficial owners per Art. 927a CO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Federal Central Tax Office (ESTV/AFC) template, completed and signed by all shareholders and beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature or certified signature by an officially recognized certifying authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank confirmation of the blocked share capital account (CHF 100,000 nominal, minimum CHF 20,000 paid-up)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss bank or notary's client escrow account confirmation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-registration screening of all directors, statutory agents, shareholders holding 10% or more, and all beneficial owners against the Swiss SECO Sanctions List, FINMA sanctions decisions, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Sanctions List, and OFAC SDN List. PEP status is assessed per AMLA Art. 4 para. 1 and FINMA Circular 2023/01, with politically exposed persons as defined in AMLA Art. 1a para. 5, including family members and close associates; any PEP relationship requires senior management approval and enhanced ongoing monitoring. Although simplified due diligence is permitted for the low-risk digital publishing segment (AMLA Art. 3 lit. a), PEP and sanctions screening is always mandatory and must be documented before the notarial deed is executed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Central Business Name Index of the Swiss Federal Commercial Register (www.zefix.ch); preliminary name clearance is conducted by the Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce) of the intended canton of the registered office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must use Roman script and correspond to an official language of Switzerland (German, French, Italian or Romansh), or contain a foreign-language element only upon demonstration of a legitimate business interest. The legal form suffix can be 'Aktiengesellschaft', 'AG', 'Societe Anonyme', 'SA', 'Societa Anonima' or 'SA'. The name must be distinctive, truthful, non-misleading and clearly distinguishable from all existing names in the Swiss Commercial Register, in accordance with CO Art. 950-951 and the Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV) Art. 14.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Swiss / Schweiz / Suisse / Svizzera / Confederation (requires prior authorization from the Federal Department of Justice and Police)
Bank / Banque / Banca (requires FINMA banking licence)
National / Federal / Eidgenoessisch / Federal (implies public authority status)
Foundation / Stiftung / Fondation (reserved for separate foundation forms)
Red Cross / Croix-Rouge / Rotes Kreuz (protected emblem)
University / Hochschule / Academy (requires cantonal education approval)
Group / Holding / Konzern (only permissible with an actual consolidated group structure)
Audit / Revision / Revisionsstelle (requires admission by the Federal Audit Oversight Authority)
Trust / Fiduciary (may require licensing under the Swiss Financial Services Act and can mislead as to regulated status)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Cantonal Commercial Register supervisory authority or the cantonal Administrative Court within 30 days of the written rejection notice, per CO Art. 970 and the applicable cantonal administrative procedure act. The applicant may alternatively file a revised name application without prejudice. The 90-day reservation may be renewed once at the discretion of the commercial register office if the incorporation file is still in preparation. On final denial, an administrative appeal to the Federal Administrative Court and ultimately the Federal Supreme Court is available. Any appeal should be accompanied by the original rejection notice, the proposed articles of association, and evidence of legitimate business interest in the contested name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Pure virtual or PO-box offices are not permissible. The AG must maintain a physical registered office in the canton of domicile per CO Art. 56, 70 and 71. The use of a regulated commercial domiciliation provider (e.g., in Zug, Zurich or Geneva) is accepted by the Commercial Register practice, and for the low-risk ISIC 5813 digital publishing scope a licensed domiciliation address satisfies the legal requirement. However, for banking KYC with Stripe and AdSense payouts, a physical service address and demonstrable operational substance are strongly recommended to avoid account freezes and enhanced due diligence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk: approximately 10% annual probability of unannounced physical inspection for a standard low-risk digital publishing AG with its own office; approximately 25-30% annual probability if a shared commercial domiciliation provider address is used, due to targeted FINMA and tax authority inspection programs for domiciliation providers.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary name clearance check for three proposed company names (Zefix and Cantonal Commercial Register)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official tariff under the Swiss Commercial Register Fee Ordinance (HRegV) - approximately CHF 60

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial certification of the deed of formation and Articles of Association
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff of the canton of registration for incorporation of an AG - approximately CHF 800

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Entry fee in the Commercial Register (federal fee plus cantonal fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office and Federal Commercial Register Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff: federal fee CHF 100 plus cantonal fee CHF 500-700 under HRegV

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation and submission of the UBO declaration to the Federal Central Tax Office (service provider fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Federal Central Tax Office (ESTV/AFC) - no statutory filing fee; preparation by licensed compliance provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for UBO filing preparation - approximately CHF 220

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of foreign documents (passport copies, certificate of good standing, corporate extracts)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal apostille authority and embassies or consulates of document origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official Hague Apostille fee schedule (CHF 30-80 per document) plus consular legalization tariffs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN, EU and SECO sanctions screening of all directors, shareholders and beneficial owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Swiss compliance provider or law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for transactional screening - approximately CHF 300

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Independent Swiss legal counsel: pre-incorporation due diligence, statute drafting, name clearance support and corporate governance advice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for AG formation legal work - approximately CHF 2,300-2,800

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of corporate documents into German, French, Italian or English
Registered office and domiciliation service - first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Regulated Swiss domiciliation provider or trust company
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for licensed domiciliation - approximately CHF 1,100-1,400 per annum

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Business bank account opening facilitation and KYC support (for Stripe and AdSense payouts)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss bank (e.g., UBS, ZKB, Zuger Kantonalbank) or regulated onboarding agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank published service tariff; fee may be waived by certain financial institutions

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory minimum share capital deposit (CHF 100,000 nominal capital, minimum CHF 20,000 paid-up in blocked escrow)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss bank or notary's client escrow account, released to the company corporate account upon registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory capital requirement under CO Art. 626 and Art. 628; this is share capital, not a fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR/CO), Arts. 620-763 as revised by the Swiss Company Law Reform effective 1 January 2023; Federal Ordinance on the Commercial Register (HRegV/ORC), Arts. 12-18; Swiss VAT Act (LTVA), Art. 10.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce) coordinated through the Swiss Federal Commercial Register Office within the Federal Department of Justice and Police; electronic filing via the EHRA/Web-Handelsregister secure portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association (Statuten / Statuts), filed electronically in the cantonal Commercial Register and published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB/SOGC).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital of CHF 100,000 is required, of which at least CHF 50,000 must be fully paid up in cash before registration; the paid-up amount must be deposited in a blocked Swiss bank account and released only after the Company obtains its Commercial Register excerpt; non-cash contributions (Sacheinlagen) require a licensed audit review and a verification report filed with the registration application.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION: (1) The issuance and full subscription of 1,000 registered shares with nominal value of one hundred Swiss francs each, constituting the entire share capital of CHF 100,000; (2) the registered office of the Company is fixed at its stated address in Zurich, Switzerland; (3) the board assumes office and appoints [Name] as Chairperson and [Name] as Secretary; (4) general signatory authority is granted to [Name] and joint signatory authority to [Name]; (5) the officers are instructed to complete the commercial registration, open the corporate bank account, register the value-added-tax number, and secure all required administrative permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary Public (Notariat / Office du notaire), e.g., Notariat Zurich
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the deed and the articles of association in German (or with a certified German translation); all founding shareholders must appear personally before the Swiss notary, produce original passports, and sign the deed in the notary's presence. The notary certifies the signatures and the instrument, and forwards the notarized deed and statutory cachet to the Commercial Register upon completion of the capital requirements.
required_dossiers: Original valid passport of each founder
Draft articles of association and deed of incorporation
Notarized power of attorney if any founder is represented
Letter of intent or lease confirmation for the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies inconsistencies or omitted signatures, the deed is corrected on site or a supplementary notarial session is scheduled; if the documents are drafted in English, a sworn German translation will be ordered and re-submitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Paid-Up Capital and Issuance of the Banker's Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank regulated by FINMA selected by the founders; account opened in the name of the company in formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked corporate account in the exact company style as set out in the deed, deposit at least CHF 50,000 of the paid-up capital, and obtain from the bank a written confirmation that the amount is irrevocably at the Company's disposal and restricted exclusively for incorporation purposes. This confirmation must match the share capital and company name set forth in the notarized deed.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation and articles of association
First board resolution and bank account opening authorization
Anti-money-laundering declaration on the origin of capital
Passport copies of all signatories and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises source-of-funds or AML questions, provide certified bank statements and a notarized declaration of the founders; the banker's confirmation must then be re-issued under an exactly matching corporate denomination before proceeding to the Commercial Register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Registration with the Cantonal Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) via the federal EHRA/Web-Handelsregister electronic filing platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized deed, the articles of association, and the banker's capital confirmation through the EHRA portal together with the electronic application in the canton of the registered office; verify that all board members have certified signatures and that no bankruptcy or insolvency proceedings exist against founders; the registrar examines the legal form, capital, seat, and purpose and, upon approval, transmits the entry to the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce for publication.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation and articles of association
Banker's confirmation of paid-up capital
Certified specimen signatures of the board members
Statutory declaration of no pending bankruptcy, liquidation, or criminal insolvency offences
Electronic application form signed with a qualified electronic signature
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a curing notice (Mängelrüge), the requested annexes must be filed within 14 days; if the deadline lapses, the application is deemed withdrawn and a fresh filing with re-payment of the registration fee is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Swiss Official Gazette Publication and Acquisition of Legal Personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB/SOGC) managed by the Federal Office of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval by the cantonal Commercial Register, the incorporation entry is published in the SOGC, including the company name, legal form, registered office, purpose, board members, and signatory powers; the Company acquires separate legal personality on the date of registration, and the blocked capital is released upon presentation of the Commercial Register excerpt.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract issued by the canton
Cantonal registration decision; no separate SHAB application is required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a publication error occurs, file a rectification request with the cantonal Commercial Register; creditors have a 30-day objection period for pre-incorporation liabilities, and any objections must be answered through the register office procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal UID, VAT, and Employer Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA/EStV) for the enterprise identifier and VAT; Central Compensation Office (ZAS) and cantonal compensation fund for AHV employer registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the company's enterprise identifier (UID) in the federal UID register and submit the VAT registration form if taxable turnover is expected to exceed CHF 100,000 annually; register with the AHV compensation fund as an employer, and, if staff will be hired, register for SUVA accident insurance and the federal withholding tax mechanism for directors and employees.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract
Value-Added-Tax registration form (EStV 201) and AHV employer registration form
Articles of association
List of directors, executive officers, and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FTA returns the application for missing information or signatures, correct and re-submit through the eService portal using a qualified electronic signature; if a VAT deadline is missed, a late-reminder fee may be imposed, and voluntary registration may be applied for retroactively where legally permissible.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Verification of Physical Premises, Zoning Compatibility, and Occupational Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal municipal authorities (Baubehörde / Service des constructions), cantonal building insurance fire-safety office (Kantonaler Gebäudeversicherung / Établissement cantonal d'assurance), and the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) in respect of digital-services supervision
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For a pure digital magazine publishing portal, no sector-specific federal industrial license is required; the officers must nevertheless verify that the registered office lease is compatible with the local zoning category, obtain a fire-safety certificate for the premises, and, if any paid sponsored media placements are offered, ensure compliance with the Swiss Unfair Competition Act (UWG) disclosure obligations and data-protection rules under the revised Federal Act on Data Protection (nFADP).
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract
Lease agreement or deed of usufruct for the registered office
Fire-safety and building-insurance clearance certificate
Statement of business purpose for zoning compatibility review
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the zoning inspection rejects the intended business use, relocate the registered office to a commercially zoned address with an appropriate reception area or apply for an administrative building permit; if the fire-safety authority issues objections, implement the prescribed structural and equipment measures and submit a new clearance application.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for a pure digital publishing service; general trade and business supervision rests with the Cantonal Commercial Register Office and the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) for digital-services regulatory oversight.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required under Swiss federal law for a digital magazine portal (ISIC 5813 / NAICS 511120); the Commercial Register entry constitutes the statutory authorization to operate, subject to ordinary municipal police and workplace norms.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical production, no fixed industrial installation, no pollutant emissions, and no environmental permit threshold triggered by the digital publishing activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the digital service itself; any leased office space must comply with the cantonal building and energy regulations (MuKEn), and waste-management duties apply only to ordinary office waste handling pursuant to the Federal Act on the Protection of the Environment (Umweltschutzgesetz).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupational safety and health in any office premises must comply with the Swiss Labour Act (ArG) and the Workplace Regulation (Verordnung 4 über Arbeits- und Schutz); a fire-safety certificate from the cantonal building insurance authority is required for commercial premises, and the employer must remit civil-defense-related social contributions to the cantonal compensation fund; no separate civil-defense clearance is required for a digital-only business operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC – Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung / Administration fédérale des contributions), VAT Main Division; electronic filing portal 'Mein ESTV / Mon AFC' at www.estv.admin.ch; cantonal/communal tax offices assess corporate income tax and capital tax (e.g., Zug/Zurich/Bern Cantonal Tax Office).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The CH_AG receives a statutory business identifier (UID – Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) upon entry in the Commercial Register (Handelsregister) issued by the Federal Statistical Office (BFS); VAT liability is then triggered by separate registration with the ESTV via the 'Mein ESTV' e-portal (VAT form 'Registrierung für die MwSt'). A foreign entity (non-resident supplier) applies for a Swiss VAT number (format CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx MWST) with a Tax Representative based in Switzerland, also through the same portal; registration is immediate from the first taxable turnover franc in the absence of a Swiss registered seat.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law provides no US-style check-the-box regime; the AG is an opaque per se corporation subject to federal, cantonal, and communal income tax plus capital tax. Material statutory elections include: (a) VAT grouping election for Swiss-based affiliates (Art. 21 MWSTG); (b) participation relief election on dividend and capital gains from qualifying shareholdings (Beteiligungsabzug); (c) Swiss tax transparency (look-through) election only for certain Swiss SICAV/partnership structures, not for an AG; (d) hybrid mismatch neutralizing elections under the Swiss implementing rules for BEPS Action 2 (anti-hybrid provisions); (e) deemed-liquidation tax election upon migration of the AG out of Switzerland.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual taxable turnover (excluding investment income) for Swiss-resident businesses; no de minimis threshold for foreign suppliers of electronically supplied B2C digital services who must register from the first CHF; CHF 10,000 threshold for acquisition tax on imported services and supplies of goods by foreign suppliers under certain conditions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance/API clearance mandate exists in Switzerland; domestic VAT invoices are issued offline, but must satisfy statutory data requirements (Kwittung/TVA invoice requirements). Switzerland participates in the Peppol framework for B2G (supply to federal administration) e-invoicing on an opt-in basis; from 2026, digital e-invoicing standards are being phased in for B2B on a voluntary basis, with no digital tax stamping requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Digital magazine sales abroad qualify for the 0% export rate (or are exempt from Swiss VAT) where the place of supply is outside Switzerland: for B2B subscriptions and sponsored-media placements, the place of supply is the customer's place of business (Art. 18(2) MWSTG) — thus no Swiss VAT is charged; for B2C private subscribers residing abroad, the place of supply is their country of habitual residence, provided the digital content is effectively consumed abroad. Google AdSense/Stripe proceeds are treated as consideration for online marketing/royalty-like services supplied to non-resident digital platforms and qualify for 0% VAT subject to proof that the platform (e.g., Google Ireland) is outside Switzerland and the reverse-charge/recipient-accounting applies. Input VAT recovery is preserved when the transaction is substantiated as an export of services per Art. 23 MWSTG.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss export customs declaration / bill of lading (CAD or NCTS) for any physical media shipments of magazines or USB storage devices
Subscriber/IP/geo-location foreign-residence report exported from the digital magazine platform (CMS logs), demonstrating consumption outside Switzerland
Payment gateway reconciliation reports (Stripe Adyen/AdSense payout summaries) showing offshore card acquirer BINs and remittance countries
Inward Remittance Certificate / Swiss bank SWIFT MT940-credit advice evidencing receipt of foreign proceeds within 180 days
License or advertising insertion orders with place-of-performance clauses and foreign customer due-diligence files
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: In cases of erroneous or fraudulent export zero-rating, the ESTV retroactively assesses Swiss VAT (8.1% or applicable reduced rate 2.6% for qualifying electronic magazines) plus default interest at 5% p.a.; deliberate or reckless VAT evasion is sanctioned with a fine of up to three times the tax evaded (Art. 96/97 MWSTG), and wilful tax fraud may lead to imprisonment. The reassessment statute of limitations is 5 years for ordinary corrections and 10 years for fraudulent suppression; clawback for wrongly deducted input VAT also triggers interest and penalties and bars the AG from future export zero-rating refunds pending resubstantiation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB; Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse), operating under the Federal Act on the National Bank and the Federal Department of Finance (FDF); no separate foreign-exchange-control authority exists, as exchange regulation is embedded in SNB monetary policy and statutory statistical-reporting powers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland grants full convertibility on both capital and current accounts under Art. 27 of the Swiss Federal Constitution and the Federal Act on Money and Payment Instruments. There are no exchange-control approvals, no prior licensing for foreign-currency purchases, and no restrictions on repatriation of share capital, dividends, interest, royalties, or liquidation proceeds. The only practical constraints for the digital magazine portal are SECO and FINMA sanctions/embargo screening duties plus CRS/FATCA reporting; the AG may freely hold, invoice, and disburse in CHF, USD, EUR, or any other currency, making profit remittance legally frictionless.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no mandatory surrender rules, statutory timelines, or conversion ratios for export proceeds. Export receipts in foreign currency may be retained indefinitely in foreign-currency accounts, converted at market rates, or netted internally. The sole residual obligation is threshold-based statistical reporting to the SNB under the National Bank Act where total foreign assets exceed CHF 100 million; digital advertising and subscription receipts below this threshold carry no reporting duty, and no conversion obligation applies to Stripe or AdSense inflows.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (blocked share-capital confirmation under Art. 622–632 Swiss Code of Obligations) plus Operational CHF/USD/EUR current account
Operational Account with automated sweeping of Stripe/AdSense payouts; Capital Escrow Account available
Operational Account (CHF/EUR current account, SEPA direct debit, SWIFT international payments)
Operational Account for media service disbursements and supplier settlements
Capital Escrow Account and private-banking cash-collateral account for shareholder loan structures

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-Low as primary banking anchor and High as auxiliary pay-in/pay-out collection rail. Offshore digital EMIs (UK FCA EMIs, Lithuanian/Luxembourg e-money institutions) may lawfully serve the AG as pass-through settlement processors for Stripe and AdSense payouts, but they cannot issue the blocked-account confirmation (girierte Einzahlung / Sperrkonto-Bestätigung) that the Swiss Commercial Register requires as proof of the paid-up CHF 100,000 minimum share capital; that instrument must originate from a FINMA-licensed bank or FinTech with a Swiss establishment. FINMA guidance further prohibits deposit-taking offshore EMIs above CHF 100 million public funds absent a Swiss FinTech licence, and EMIs do not have direct access to Swiss SIC clearing, necessitating a licensed correspondent arrangement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG) and the Due Diligence Agreement CDB 20, the bank must identify the legal entity and its beneficial owner. Physical presence of at least one signatory director is generally required for first onboarding of an AG; UBS and ZKB, however, accept remote video-verified KYC interviews where the beneficial-ownership chain is straightforward and the industry risk tier is Low_Risk_Standard. Non-resident directors without Swiss residence must provide notarized board minutes, apostillized passport copies, a six-month source-of-funds trail covering share capital, and CRS/FATCA self-certifications; best practice is a Swiss-resident director or licensed trustee attending the Zurich or Geneva branch in person for the account-opening hearing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fragmented multi-source digital revenue aggregating over CHF 50,000 per month from Stripe, Google AdSense, and direct sponsorship insertions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform payout statements (Stripe connected-account reports, Google AdSense reconciliation), signed sponsorship insertion orders, editorial-contract VAT invoices, a board-approved revenue ledger mapping each transaction to a published magazine issue, and publication screenshots substantiating genuine editorial activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident parent holding structure with opaque ultimate beneficial owners or bearer-share arrangements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete CH_AG share register under Art. 686ff. Code of Obligations listing all registered shareholders, CDB 20 Form A/B beneficial-owner declarations, apostillized certificates of incorporation for each intermediate entity, and an ownership diagram extending to ultimate natural persons; conversion of any bearer shares into registered shares to satisfy CDB/GoAML screening expectations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound royalty or licence disbursements to content licensors and media agencies situated in non-treaty or sanctioned-adjacent jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed licence agreements with standard indemnity provisions, Swiss transfer-pricing documentation applying OECD arm's-length principles, counterparty tax-residency certificates, negative-media and OFAC/EU/SECO sanctions screening reports on every payee, and force-majeure/sanctions-termination clauses in the underlying media contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid capital injection followed by repayment to the shareholder within 12 months (round-tripping/cash-farming red flag)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution authorizing the capital increase, blocked-account bank confirmation evidencing the paid-in CHF 100,000 minimum under Art. 632 Code of Obligations, a business-plan cash-flow forecast demonstrating working-capital deployment for magazine development and platform settlement cycles, and contractual evidence of operating expenses corresponding to the injected funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route via SWIFT MT103 with purpose narrative 'Einzahlung Aktienkapital / Capital contribution CH_AG' and, for Swiss statistical-reporting classifications, the code corresponding to equity contribution; CHF-denominated injections clear through SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) for same-day finality directly into the blocked capital-escrow account. Cross-border USD/EUR founder contributions clear via SIX Interbank Clearing correspondents using MT103/MT202 with a unique reference to the escrow account. The Commercial Register requires a bank-generated blocked-funds confirmation (Bestätigung Art. 15 OR) rather than notarization of the wire itself; the bank verifies the ledger entry and issues the confirmation only after value-date settlement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: CHF domestic disbursements use SIC with immediate finality; EUR payouts to EEA/EU suppliers and affiliate networks use SEPA Credit Transfer settling in T2/TARGET2; non-EEA international payments, including licensing fees to content licensors and cloud/hosting disbursements to AWS and Cloudflare, execute via SWIFT MT103. For large media procurement exceeding CHF 100,000, an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP 600) with MT700 issuance or a standby LC is required; documentary collections (URC 522) are reserved for high-risk counterparties. Stripe and AdSense payouts are received through local acquiring rails and swept nightly via SEPA/SIC into the UBS operational account, preserving a segregated audit trail between gross media revenue and operating disbursements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forward (deliverable CHF/USD/EUR, onshore Swiss counterparty; no requirement under Swiss law to prove an underlying transaction)
FX Swap (swap/rollover instrument for short-term liquidity and cross-currency reconciliation of advertising receipts)
Plain Vanilla European FX Options (OTC purchases for downside protection on USD-denominated AdSense revenue)
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swap (XCCY) converting EUR advertising receivable streams into CHF liability profiles

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on referenced emerging-market currencies solely for content-licensor settlement exposure, booked through a Swiss-authorized bank; NDFs on the freely convertible CHF are excluded from permissible usage

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (direct federal tax, cantonal tax, and cantonal capital tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration of the registered office; Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) for the direct federal tax share
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end (calendar-year companies generally by May–September, depending on canton); extensions are available upon written request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on late tax at 4.5% to 5.5% p.a.; procedural fine up to CHF 5,000; if filings remain pending, the tax authority will issue a tax assessment by estimation and may initiate administrative collection proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT settlement return and declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the expiry of the settlement period; settlement periods are annual, semi-annual, or quarterly depending on taxable turnover and prior filing behavior
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 5% p.a.; administrative fines up to CHF 8,000 for VAT violations; systematic non-filing may result in tax reassessment by summary taxation and criminal proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and mandatory audit report for the shareholders' ordinary general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Meeting of Shareholders (no public filing for non-listed companies unless ordinary audit is required; audited financial statements must be retained and made available on request)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Board of directors must prepare and approve the annual report within 6 months of the balance sheet date and submit it to the annual general meeting in that period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Breach of directors' duties under Art. 754 CO; civil liability for losses; non-adoption of financial statements may trigger a review by the commercial register authority and, in extreme cases, a court order to convene the general meeting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual share register and UBO record maintenance confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors (internal statutory register; not publicly filed with a government agency)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuously updated upon any share transfer; the board must confirm compliance at each annual general meeting and maintain the register at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Violation of Arts. 686–697l CO exposes officers to liability; failure to accurately maintain beneficial-owner records under Swiss AMLA may lead to fines up to CHF 500,000 and audit by the cantonal banking or financial-market supervisory body

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An ordinary audit is mandatory for Aktiengesellschaften exceeding two of the following three thresholds in two consecutive financial years: total assets CHF 20 million, gross turnover CHF 40 million, and 250 full-time employees. Ordinary audit also is required for listed companies, licensees under the Financial Services Act, and companies where shareholders holding at least 10% of share capital request an audit. Smaller AGs may be subject to a limited (review) audit unless all shareholders agree in writing to full audit exemption.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957 et seq.) applying Swiss GAAP FER as the primary national framework; IFRS or US GAAP permitted for listed or consolidated groups; no separate local tax basis is required but the annual financial statements form the starting point for tax assessment.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland does not maintain a public annual UBO filing system. Non-listed AGs must record in the share register the full legal name, address, nationality, and shareholding percentage of each shareholder, and must identify the ultimate beneficial owners where shares are held in nominee or trust structures. The register must be updated immediately upon share transfers and annually confirmed by the board in its resolution preceding the ordinary general meeting. The confirmation is subject to inspection by bailiffs, social-security authorities, and financial-intermediary AML officers.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of the General Meeting and Board of Directors

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800–5,000 (typical annual US$/CHF equivalent for registered office and corporate agent services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500–9,000 (typical annual US$ equivalent fee for a statutory limited or ordinary audit by a licensed Swiss audit firm)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% (Federal Direct Tax on legal entities; plus cantonal/communal rates varying by seat, typical aggregate effective rate 12%-18%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains; R&D super-deduction up to 150% in many cantons; patent box relief for qualifying IP income; notional interest deduction on equity in certain cantons; cantonal tax holidays obtainable for new job-creating activities on a case-by-case basis.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined Swiss Federal and Cantonal Corporate Income Tax Return (Formular für juristische Personen / Formulaire pour personnes morales); filed via the official electronic portal of the competent Cantonal Tax Office; ESTV federal tax assessment adopts the cantonal filing and tax base.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Cantonal deadline generally falling 6 months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., 30 June for a 31 December balance sheet); extensions are available on request; Federal Direct Tax assessment follows the cantonal filing cycle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit per statutory annual financial statements (commercial income statement under Swiss Code of Obligations)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter Swiss standalone annual profit; do not consolidate foreign subsidiaries; amounts in CHF.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses (federal/cantonal income taxes, provisions exceeding commercial requirements, donations above deductible ceiling, excessive representation costs, interest on hidden equity)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply add-backs identically to a Swiss-owned AG; no special foreign-owner exclusion exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction for participation income (dividends and capital gains on qualifying shareholdings of at least 10% or CHF 1 million acquisition cost)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must attach proof of participation and, if treaty benefits are claimed, evidence of beneficial ownership and substance in the investee.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Special deductions: R&D super-deduction, patent box relief, notional interest deduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Substantiate with contemporaneous R&D registers, IP-holding documentation and financing calculations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carryforward from prior seven assessment episodes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only unexpired losses in chronological order; losses cannot be carried back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after exemptions and deductions forming the federal 8.5% direct tax base and the cantonal/communal tax base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute in CHF; foreign parent should not divert Swiss-source profit by accounting policy; transfer pricing documentation must support all intercompany margins.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file timely triggers an estimated assessment (Einschätzungsverfahren), default interest at 3.5% p.a., and procedural fines generally CHF 100-10,000 under cantonal/federal procedural law; deliberate false filing initiates criminal tax proceedings carrying fines up to 3x evaded tax and imprisonment in qualified cases.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss Federal Anticipatory Withholding Tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on gross dividends distributed by the Swiss AG.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Payer must withhold 35%; foreign shareholder applies to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) on Form 823 for relief at source or refund; submission requires a valid certificate of tax residence (TRC) issued by the shareholder's home tax authority, proof of qualified shareholding, beneficial ownership declaration, and Swiss withholding tax declaration; processing typically 2-4 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: bundled public-debt interest (Obligationenzinsen) paid by the Swiss AG is subject to 35% withholding tax; royalties and ordinary intercompany/bank loan interest are not subject to Swiss source withholding tax. Treaty rates: interest generally 0-10% (commonly 0%); royalties generally 0-10% depending on DTA; where no WHT applies domestically, no DTA reduction procedure is necessary.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss law does not impose a fixed statutory Local File/Master File threshold; administrative practice expects a Local File when annual cross-border related-party transactions exceed CHF 1 million and a Master File for MNE groups with consolidated revenue above CHF 500 million. Contemporaneous documentation must be available in all material intercompany transactions to avoid audit adjustments.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Cayman-style Economic Substance Regulations do not apply; however Swiss anti-abuse rules, substance-over-form case law, the OECD Multilateral Instrument beneficial ownership test, and the effective management doctrine impose substance requirements on a Swiss AG (physical office, trained personnel, substantive board meetings, local decision-making, and proper accounting records) for corporate residence, treaty access, and transfer pricing defense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-reporting digital advertising and subscription revenues from Stripe and AdSense payouts, or claiming fictitious editorial/post-production costs to reduce Swiss taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of evaded tax plus default interest, and fine up to three times the tax evaded under Art. 175 DBG; repeated or collusive conduct escalates to criminal tax prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed a false return are personally exposed to fines and criminal sanctions; Swiss veil-piercing principles and Art. 754 OR permit recovery of corporate tax debts from wilful or negligent board members.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting forged advertising invoices, backdated sponsorship contracts, or using a sham digital publishing intermediary solely to generate artificial deductions and to conceal taxable revenues.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment up to five years and/or fine under Art. 186 DBG; loss of all statute-of-limitation defenses; full tax re-assessment and denial of treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Executive board members are criminally liable as principals; civil restitution orders, seizure of personal assets, and travel bans may be imposed during proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging a 30%+ royalty or service margin from the Swiss AG to a foreign affiliate without benchmarking, or maintaining intercompany receivables carrying no interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax audit adjustment increasing Swiss taxable income, 3.5% default interest, and administrative penalties; serious intentional misstatement leads to criminal prosecution for tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors responsible for incomplete transfer-pricing documentation face civil liability for additional taxes and audit costs; negligence under Art. 754 OR may also support third-party creditor claims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the magazine portal as a domiciliary shell with only a registered address, no Swiss editorial staff, no board decision-making in Switzerland, and no real substantive activity while claiming Swiss residence and treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Rebuttal of corporate seat/effective management; retroactive domicile shift abroad; denial of DTA relief; reassessment of hidden reserves and deemed dividends; administrative fines up to CHF 10,000 and possible dissolution proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Swiss 'Durchgriff' doctrine, aggrieved tax authorities and creditors may pierce the corporate veil and pursue directors and shareholders personally; individuals may face travel bans and forced-liquidation cooperation orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting programmatic-advertising deposits or affiliate payouts through the AG without implementing Switzerland's Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG) identification and record-keeping procedures, or allowing the digital magazine portal to be used as an undisclosed pass-through for third-party advertising funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to CHF 500,000 under GwG for entities; aggravated violations carry imprisonment up to five years; FINMA may strike financial-intermediary registrations; internal controls are deemed deficient.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML officers, compliance directors, and board members acting with wilful blindness face direct criminal conviction, personal fines, asset freezes, and civil restitution obligations toward creditors and the bankruptcy estate.
